warrior_bloodthirst.notes: Also applies a self-buff: +10% movement speed for 10s. The Fury talent-tree flavor text describes this ability as "35% AP + 30" (a flat bonus); the spell's own tooltip (this entry) says 35% AP + 100% SP instead. Used the spell tooltip as authoritative, per this project's standing rule that a rendered spell tooltip beats talent-tree description text when they disagree.

warrior_whirlwind.notes: Strikes with the off-hand weapon too only if Raging Blows is talented -- not automatic from dual-wielding alone (confirmed on Raging Blows' own tooltip; this was a real bug in an earlier version of the DPS simulator, fixed 2026-09-23).

warrior_heroic_strike.notes: This is the level-60 MAX rank, not the level-20-trainable rank (see gaps). "Yellow" special attack, not a boosted white swing -- confirmed via the community's attack-table research (Vanilla WoW Wiki): no dual-wield miss penalty, no glancing blow. Icy Veins' level-20 guide explicitly says to generally avoid this ability while leveling since Rage income is too low for it to be efficient at that stage.

warrior_rend.notes: Rank 3 is exactly the level-20 cap (Requires level 20). Rank 1 (wowhead_spell_id 772, level 4): 10 Rage, 15 dmg/9s (5/tick). Rank 2 (wowhead_spell_id 6546, level 10): 10 Rage, 28 dmg/12s (7/tick). Unlike this project's earlier generic-bleed assumption used elsewhere, Rend's own tooltip explicitly flags "Periodic Can Crit" -- a real mechanic, not an assumption.

warrior_sunder_armor.notes: Reduces the TARGET's armor, which only translates into a DPS gain via a real armor-mitigation formula and a known target armor value -- neither sourced yet (see gaps). Wowhead lists 4 further "ranks" but they're tagged as hidden/scaling changes, not player-trainable ranks, so max_rank_total is 1 here.

warrior_overpower.notes: Only usable for a few seconds after the CURRENT target dodges one of your attacks -- directly relevant now that this project's DPS simulator already models a real Dodge chance against a boss. The tooltip also displayed a stray "1 to 5 Combo Points" cost fragment, which is a Rogue resource and almost certainly a Wowhead template artifact for this ID, not a real Warrior mechanic -- ignored, not included in resource_cost.

warrior_bloodrage.notes: 20 Rage total (10 instant + 10 over 10s) for 20% of base Health, no GCD, 1-minute cooldown.

warrior_battle_shout.notes: Rank 1 shown; exact rank trainable at level 20 not cross-checked against the other 6 ranks (see gaps).

warrior_charge.notes: Also stuns the target for 1 sec (Charge Stun). Cannot be used once already in combat -- for a sustained single-target fight, this only ever fires once, at the very start, as a small opening Rage boost. Description text says 9 Rage; the raw tooltip effect value shows 10 -- used the description text as authoritative, per this project's standing rule for these tooltip-internal discrepancies. Ranks 2/3 exist but weren't checked (see gaps).

warrior_victory_rush.notes: OUT OF SCOPE for a sustained single-target DPS simulator: it can only be used within 20 seconds of killing a (non-trivial) enemy, which never happens in a continuous single-boss fight -- the same reason Execute is out of scope at level 60. Real and correctly used in Icy Veins' leveling rotation (where kills happen constantly), just not applicable to this project's fight model.

warrior_demoralizing_shout.notes: OUT OF SCOPE for DPS output: this reduces the ENEMY's attack power (how hard it hits the player), not the player's own damage -- a pure survivability/threat tool with zero effect on the number this project's simulator measures. Rank 1 (this entry) is the max rank available by level 20; Rank 2 requires level 24 (wowhead_spell_id 6190, -91 AP instead of -63). Real and correctly used in Icy Veins' leveling rotation for survivability, not DPS.

warrior_slam.notes: Rank 1, exactly the level-20 cap (real Forever spell id, distinct from the level-30 Rank 2 id=1464 -- do not confuse the two, they were briefly mixed up while sourcing this entry). Real, sourced Arms-vs-Fury rotation difference (Icy Veins' own Arms and Fury level-20 guides are word-for-word identical except for this one bullet): Arms' rotation explicitly includes 'Slam right after an auto-attack' as a filler (it has a cast time, so timing it right after a landed white swing minimizes lost time and resets that swing's timer); Fury's own guide does NOT include Slam in its priority list at all, despite it being trainable by any Warrior at level 20 -- a real, deliberate omission per the source, not something to add to Fury's rotation.

paladin_holy_strike.notes: Exactly the level-20 cap. Base 12-second cooldown; Improved Holy Strike (talented in the primary real build) reduces this. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): use on cooldown alongside Judgement, whenever Mana allows.

effects.description: Deals whatever damage/effect the currently active Seal's own "Judgement effect" specifies -- see the active Seal's own ability entry.

paladin_judgement.notes: Real, important mechanic: Judgement deals NO damage of its own -- it "unleashes the energy of your active Seal" without consuming it, so its actual effect comes entirely from whichever Seal ability's own entry is active (see paladin_seal_of_righteousness for the default single-target Seal). Costs a % of base Mana, not a flat amount. Uses no GCD, unlike almost every other ability catalogued in this project so far.

effects.notes: scales with weapon speed: slower weapons get more bonus damage per swing

effects.description: When Judgement is cast while this Seal is active

paladin_seal_of_righteousness.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 26). Two distinct effects in one ability: (1) a passive buff, active for 30s, adding +6 to 20 Holy damage to every melee swing (explicitly weapon-speed-scaled: "slower weapons cause more Holy damage per swing" -- a real per-swing flat bonus, not a DPS-normalized one); (2) a separate 53-57 Holy damage direct hit dealt only when Judgement is cast while this Seal is active ("unleashing this Seal's energy"). Real, explicit tooltip rule: "Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time" -- another sourced non-stacking-across-sources rule, consistent with Serpent Sting's (Hunter) similar rule. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): the default Seal to keep active unless Seal of Command is talented (not in this build).

paladin_consecration.notes: Exactly the level-20 cap (real Forever redesign: trained from the Paladin trainer rather than a talent, per the source). Real single-target priority (Protection, Icy Veins): the top rotation priority, kept up on cooldown. Real tooltip: 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to any enemy standing in the area, with the FIRST 4 enemies taking an additional 32 damage over 8 sec (a multi-target bonus, not modeled here -- solo single-target value only). Duration and cooldown are identical (8s), so it can be kept at 100% uptime. Tick cadence within the 8s wasn't explicitly confirmed on the raw tooltip (its own effect breakdown showed unrelated threat/script values, not a clean per-tick damage number) -- 4 ticks of 4 assumed as the closest classic-Consecration-consistent reading of "16 over 8 sec", disclosed rather than left unmodeled.

hunter_aimed_shot.notes: Exactly the level-20 cap (this is the ability's very first rank). Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): use on cooldown, after Serpent Sting.

hunter_serpent_sting.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 26). Real, explicit tooltip rule: "Only one Sting per Hunter can be active on any one target" -- a sourced non-stacking-across-sources rule distinct from (but compatible with) this schema's general refresh-not-stack default. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): cast once the pet has engaged, before Aimed Shot.

hunter_arcane_shot.notes: Exactly the level-20 cap. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): only cast "if you have extra mana", otherwise stick to Auto Shot -- an explicitly conditional, not on-cooldown, rotation piece (mana-limited, unlike Aimed Shot).

rogue_sinister_strike.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 22). Real finding validating the schema on this class: Rogue's own GCD is 1 second, not the 1.5 seconds already confirmed for Warrior and Mage -- the schema already supports this correctly (gcd_sec is per-ability, not a hardcoded constant), this is the first real confirmation it differs by class.

rogue_backstab.notes: Rank 3 is exactly the level-20 cap. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins) uses this over Sinister Strike whenever positioned behind the target -- higher combo-point-per-Energy value (60 Energy/1 CP vs Sinister Strike's 45 Energy/1 CP) is offset by the higher direct damage, not by CP generation rate.

rogue_eviscerate.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 24). Real per-combo-point damage table from the tooltip, not derived: 1 CP 25-39, 2 CP 44-58, 3 CP 63-77, 4 CP 82-96, 5 CP 101-115 (a clean +19 per point pattern, but the table itself is the sourced value, not the pattern). Also scales with Attack Power per the tooltip's own text; exact coefficient not captured this pass (see gaps).

rogue_slice_and_dice.notes: Rank 1 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 2 requires level 42). A flat +20% melee attack speed buff whose DURATION scales with combo points spent (a genuinely linear real formula, unlike Eviscerate's damage table): 1 CP=9s, 2 CP=12s, 3 CP=15s, 4 CP=18s, 5 CP=21s (base 6 + 3×CP). Per this schema's non-stacking rule, recasting while active replaces the remaining duration, it does not add to it.

priest_shadow_word_pain.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 26). Real single-target priority (Icy Veins) applies this after Mind Blast, near the end of a short fight -- consistent with a DoT that needs time to pay off.

priest_mind_blast.notes: Rank 2 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 3 requires level 22). Real single-target priority (Icy Veins) casts this right after Smite (the opener) and before Shadow Word: Pain.

priest_smite.notes: A Holy-school spell, not Shadow -- real, sourced quirk of the level-20 rotation: Shadowform (the capstone that would make Shadow spells the whole kit) is nowhere near reachable at 11 points, so Icy Veins' real rotation opens with this basic Holy nuke rather than a Shadow spell. Rank 1 is confirmed the max reachable by level 20 (the only other rank found, id 1004, requires level 30); ranks between weren't individually checked, so max_rank_total is left descriptive rather than a confirmed number.

shaman_earth_shock.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 24). Also interrupts spellcasting and locks out that school for 2 sec -- a secondary utility effect alongside the damage. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): cast when solo (Frost Shock is the group alternative, to avoid pulling threat). Shares its 6s cooldown with every other Shock spell (Flame Shock, Frost Shock) -- a well-documented core Shaman mechanic, not a per-spell cooldown (cooldown_group added 2026-09-26, user-flagged).

shaman_rockbiter_weapon.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 24). A 60-minute weapon-imbue buff (+118 melee Attack Power), not a rotational damage ability -- more like a long-duration maintenance buff (comparable in role to Warrior's Battle Shout) than a spell recast on cooldown. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): use when solo; Flametongue Weapon is the group alternative (not sourced).

shaman_lightning_bolt.notes: Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): pull with this, then return to it as filler between Flame Shock applications. Rank 1's own confirmed tooltip used (level 1) -- community data suggests a much higher rank (~49-57 damage) is the real level-20 cap, but its exact spell id wasn't pinned down this pass (disclosed conservative approximation, see gaps).

shaman_flame_shock.notes: Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): apply immediately after the Lightning Bolt pull, refresh on long-lived targets once it ends. Rank 1's own confirmed tooltip used (level 10) -- a higher rank is real level-20 cap per Call of Flame's own +5% buff to it existing at 20, but the exact intermediate rank wasn't pinned down this pass (disclosed conservative approximation, see gaps). Shares its 6s cooldown with every other Shock spell (Earth Shock, Frost Shock) -- a well-documented core Shaman mechanic, not a per-spell cooldown (cooldown_group added 2026-09-26, user-flagged).

shaman_searing_totem.notes: User-flagged (2026-09-26): untalented ("trees": []) and trainable at level 10, so available regardless of spec -- next rank is level 30, so Rank 1 is the real level-20 cap, no intermediate rank exists. Real tooltip: 'Summons a Searing Totem with 5 health at your feet for 30 sec that repeatedly attacks an enemy within 20 yards for 9 to 11 Fire damage.' Modeled here as a periodic_damage effect attributed to the caster (the engine has no separate pet/totem damage-source model, same simplification already disclosed for Hunter/Warlock pets) -- midpoint of the 9-11 range used per tick. The totem's own attack INTERVAL isn't shown on its spell tooltip (it's the summoned unit's own attack speed, not a caster cast time); 2 seconds is the commonly-cited Classic-era value across community sources (Wowpedia, classic theorycrafting), not independently confirmed on a Wowhead tooltip -- disclosed approximation, not a real per-tick sourced number like the rest of this file. No Spell Power scaling: real Searing Totem is a flat-damage totem in Classic-style itemization, never SP-scaled.

mage_fireball.notes: Rank 4 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 5 requires level 24). Real Forever design: Fireball has a built-in DoT component (not the case in original vanilla WoW) -- two effects in one cast, which is why this glossary's "effects" field is an array, not a single object (found while validating the schema on this class).

mage_fire_blast.notes: Rank 2 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 3 requires level 22). Base cooldown is 8s; Wake of Fire (talented) reduces this to 6s.

mage_pyroblast.notes: Icy Veins' level-20 guide uses this as the Single-Target Rotation opener (Fireball before level 20, when Pyroblast isn't trained yet).

mage_frostbolt.notes: A base Mage spell available to every spec, not Fire/Frost/Arcane-tree-exclusive -- both the Arcane and Frost level-20 guides name it as their real castable filler. Also applies a 6-sec, 39% movement-slow debuff (not modeled as damage). Real Rank 4 is the level-20 cap (wow-forever.gg's rank ladder); Rank 3's own confirmed tooltip (Requires level 14) is used here as a disclosed close approximation -- see gaps.

warlock_corruption.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (next found rank, id 11672, requires level 54 -- there may be an untested rank in between). Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): apply after Immolate, one of the two "always up" DoTs alongside it.

warlock_immolate.notes: Exactly the level-20 cap. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): the first DoT applied, before Corruption.

warlock_shadow_bolt.notes: Real single-target priority (Destruction only, per Icy Veins): the primary direct-damage filler, cast after Immolate/Corruption are up. Explicitly NOT part of Affliction's own rotation (see the class-level gaps note -- Affliction's own guide calls it worse than wanding at this level). Rank 1's own confirmed tooltip used (level 1); the real level-20-trainable rank is higher (a Rank 12 exists at level 60) but wasn't pinned down to a specific id this pass -- disclosed conservative approximation.

druid_wrath.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 22). Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): filler damage once Moonfire is already active on the target.

druid_moonfire.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 22). Real, sourced Arcane school (not Nature) despite being a "lunar fire" spell -- don't assume school from flavor. The tooltip's own "DoT Stacking Rule" flag is a direct, explicit confirmation of this schema's general non-stacking-on-refresh rule (see README.md), not just an inference. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): keep this active on the target at all times, ahead of Wrath.

druid_claw.notes: Exactly the level-20 cap (Cat Form itself is unlocked by a level-20 class quest). Cat Form's real combo-point builder: 110% weapon damage + 27 flat, awards 1 combo point (tooltip text; the raw effect value shows 2, tooltip text used as authoritative per this project's standing rule). Real GCD is 1 second, same as Rogue's (not the 1.5s default).

druid_rip.notes: Exactly the level-20 cap. Real per-combo-point DoT table from the tooltip (not derived): 1 CP 44 over 12s, 2 CP 71, 3 CP 97, 4 CP 124, 5 CP 150 (6 ticks of ~2s each). Real, explicit "DoT Stacking Rule" flag confirms the schema's non-stacking-on-refresh default. Real single-target priority (Wowhead's own Level 20 Feral Druid DPS guide, more precise than Icy Veins' generic text): cast at 4+ combo points if the target will live at least ~6 more seconds, otherwise keep using Claw. Also scales with Attack Power per the tooltip's own text; exact coefficient not shown in the effect breakdown (gap, same as Rogue's Eviscerate).

druid_maul.notes: Real level-10 rank (well below the level-20 cap, already usable). Bear Form's real Rage-spender: enhances the next melee swing by a flat +18 damage (tooltip text; raw effect value shows 19). No GCD -- queues onto the next swing rather than consuming an action, the same real mechanic as Warrior's Heroic Strike. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins): the main Rage dump while tanking single targets (Swipe is the AoE alternative, out of scope here).
